findings.title: A field name with HTML runs as script on the offer card, also in the seller's own My Offers
A deleted account's token still creates fields; the next registered user inherits them and the deleted account's live offer
One long word in an offer description stretches every buyer's Marketplace page sideways
Double-clicking Create Offer sends two requests and shows Error next to Success; no loading state on a slow connection
The Item dropdown offers items that are already listed
When the session ends elsewhere, Create Offer redirects to login without a message and the typed offer is lost
Description rules invisible until submit; the invalid-characters message does not say which character
Offer card heading shows 'field #id' / 'animal #id' instead of the item name; description line breaks collapsed
The Create Offer form refuses prices below 1 (known)
Letters outside the Polish alphabet (é, ü, ß) and decomposed Polish letters are refused as invalid description characters
A description sent as a JSON array bypasses the 300-character limit and is stored as an array
On a 375 px screen the Marketplace tab bar is wider than the screen; the page scrolls sideways
Any price is accepted without a check; one offer takes over the shared TOTAL VALUE header
The status dot covers the end of the price on every offer card

assumptions: Unattended run: plan not approved by a human.
Double submit and stale dropdown are routine actions but store nothing wrong: rated minor, not major.
AC-1 'a message naming the problem' is met by 'Description contains invalid characters'; the missing hint is reported as UX.
Price with 3 decimals blocked by the browser is accepted as intended (API rounds to 2 dp).
The deleted-account probe ran last; a sink account absorbed the reused user id immediately.
lessons: A POST /login replaces the user's previous token: cookie-login with the register token, never log the same user in again in a test that keeps using the old token.
Once the Create Offer tab is open there are two 'Create Offer' buttons; scope the submit to #createOfferForm.
Toasts can be captured reliably with a MutationObserver installed before the click (6 s lifetime, max 3).
struggles: pwcli: `run-code` output echoes the whole code, including the session token in the cookie-login script; piped it through `tail -1` and kept such output out of artifacts.

pwcli: `run-code --filename` code runs in the browser-driver context without `process`; a script using process.env failed with 'ReferenceError: process is not defined' after its click had already fired, which created an unintended offer (1572). Workaround: inline absolute paths; the stray offer is recorded in ui-cases-log.txt and not used as evidence.
pwcli: `console error` is cumulative per page load, so later console files repeat earlier errors and several 0-error files are byte-identical; documented in the Console section.
env: re-logging the seller through POST /login (to get loginTime) invalidated the register token used by the probes (403); added relogin.mjs that stores the new token.

reviewer: pwcli: `run-code` with an inline function that used `document` outside `page.evaluate` failed with "ReferenceError: document is not defined" (own mistake). Workaround: DOM reads inside `page.evaluate`, longer code in a file via `--filename`.

reviewer: pwcli: `locator.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded` failed "Element is not attached to the DOM" right after a create, because My Offers re-renders. Workaround: wait ~1 s, locate the card by `button[data-offer-id]`.
reviewer: pwcli: default viewport is 1280x720 while the tester used 1366x768; set it explicitly with `page.setViewportSize` in `run-code` for layout checks.
reviewer: no env problems; finished in ~40 min.

writer: `toShowFields` (src/assertions/ui-matchers.ts) reads innerText, which includes hidden (display:none) elements; a card in an unopened tab passed every field (poison P6). Added an explicit toBeVisible; the shared matcher deserves a follow-up.

writer: the Marketplace builds the Item list only when Item Type changes, from /fields and /animals loaded once at page load; on a slow network an early pick leaves the list empty for good. goto() waits for both responses. The handoff named the once-per-load read but not this timing trap.
writer: with a broken session cookie the page redirects to login before requesting fields, so goto() waits out the 30 s test timeout instead of failing fast (poison P8).
writer: handoff recipe, locators and payloads were correct; used `.marketplace-tabs` + getByRole('button', { name }) instead of `.tab-button[data-tab]`.
test-reviewer: could not find stability or poison evidence in the run folder; they live only in the writer's reply. The intent card carries them.
